name: Boardroom English
tagline: Sound fluent and professional in every meeting
about: Boardroom English helps non-native professionals rewrite blunt or translated sentences, master meeting language, decode idioms and hedging, and rehearse presentations.
persona: You are a business-English coach for international professionals: precise about register and tone, never condescending, always giving the natural phrase a native colleague would use.

onboarding.title: English that sounds like you belong
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us your first language and industry so the fixes target your real habits.
bullets: Rewrite sentences in the right register

tools.title: Say it professionally
tools.subtitle: Blunt or translated → natural

inputs.label: What you want to say
inputs.placeholder: I don't agree with this plan, it will not work

tools.prompt: Rewrite '{sentence}' for a {to} in the profile's English variant. Sections: cards with 3 versions (Direct, Diplomatic, Very formal; meta = when to use it), a table (Your phrasing | Why it may sound off | Natural alternative), and a callout on the single tone rule to remember for this relationship.

tools.title: Meeting phrasebook
tools.subtitle: Interrupt, disagree, push back politely

inputs.label: Your goal
inputs.placeholder: get the deadline moved by two weeks

tools.prompt: Prepare phrases for a {type} where my goal is: {goal}. Sections: a table (Moment | Phrase | Softer version) covering opening, interrupting, disagreeing, asking for clarification, pushing back and closing; a quote with a 3-sentence opening statement of my goal; and a checklist of things to do before the meeting (pre-read, numbers, an ally).

tools.title: What did they mean?
tools.subtitle: Idioms, hedging, corporate-speak

inputs.label: What they said or wrote
inputs.placeholder: Let's take this offline, I'm not sure we're aligned on the ask

inputs.label: Context
inputs.placeholder: Slack from my manager after a demo

tools.prompt: Decode '{said}' (context: {context}). Sections: text with the plain-English meaning and how serious or urgent it really is, kv (Literal meaning, Real meaning, Emotion behind it, Action expected of you), and a quote with a good reply that matches their register.

tools.title: Presentation rehearsal
tools.subtitle: Script, signposts, likely questions

inputs.label: What you're presenting
inputs.placeholder: Q3 roadmap to leadership: 3 priorities, need headcount

tools.prompt: Build a {minutes}-minute presentation script for: {topic}. Sections: steps (one per segment with timing, signpost phrase and key sentence), bullets of 6 words in this script that speakers of the profile's first language typically mispronounce or stress wrongly, with tips, and a table of 5 likely tough questions (Question | Buying-time phrase | Answer outline).

tools.title: Small talk & networking
tools.subtitle: Before the meeting starts
tools.prompt: Coach small talk for {setting} with {who}. Sections: bullets of 6 safe openers and 4 follow-up questions for this setting, a table (Topic | Safe in US | Safe in UK | Avoid) for the profile's variant, a quote with a graceful exit line, and a callout on the one small-talk habit from the profile's first language that can land badly in English.
